archetype: Fire magician built around a stance toggle: Fires of Creation summons either Blazing Lion or Flame Fox, and Orbital Flame, Towering Inferno and Blazing Extinction each behave differently depending on which is out. Damage is concentrated in a burst window.

linkSkill.name: Cygnus Blessing (Magician)
linkSkill.effect: At master level: +35 Attack Power and Magic ATT, +22 Abnormal Status Resistance, +22% All Elemental Resistance. Stacks once per unique Cygnus Knights job character on the world, up to five stacks.

independenceModel.note: Labelling rule applied to every endgame claim in this file on 2026-09-12. sourceCount counts INDEPENDENT LINEAGES, not pages. consensus follows mechanically: 1 lineage = weak, 2 = moderate, 3+ = strong. No Blaze Wizard endgame claim reaches 3, so nothing in the five endgame sections is labelled strong.
lineages: Arsonist's Cookbook family - the class doc itself, grandislibrary.com's Blaze Wizard page, and TajMaJon's video. Verified 2026-09-12: Grandis credits 'Class Doc' directly under the heading 'Inner Ability + Hyper Passive Build + Boost Nodes Build', so for those three fields Grandis is a restatement and counts once with the doc.
mystyjl's cross-class NodeGuide - genuinely outside the class-doc lineage, but self-reports last updated November 21st, 2024.

maplestorywiki.net - factual only (names, level requirements, numbers). Carries no recommendation, so it corroborates that a claim's nouns and numbers are real but never raises a judgement claim's sourceCount.
MathBro's Hyper Stat Optimizer - a tool, cited only to support the position that hyper stats are computed per character.

priority.node: Unlock every node at level 1 before levelling anything
priority.why: Step 1 of the class doc's Node Leveling Priority, verbatim: 'Unlock everything at level 1', with the sub-point 'Can choose to prioritize Decent Holy Symbol and Erda Shower earlier for farming'.

priority.node: Boost nodes - the first four groupings only
priority.why: Step 2 of the same list, verbatim: 'Boost Nodes / (first four) / Last two can be ignored, not part of any boost'. The doc does not name which skills sit in which grouping - the skill icons are images.
priority.consensusNote: Downgraded from moderate on 2026-09-12. The second page previously counted here (Grandis Library) credits the class doc for its Boost Nodes Build, so it is the same lineage, not a second vote.

priority.why: Step 3 of the class doc's levelling order, after boost nodes and before common nodes. The ordering line inside this step reads 'Prioritize [icon] followed by [icon] and [icon], then [icon]' - the skill names are inline images and are absent from the text layer, so no order is recorded. The four Blaze Wizard class skill nodes the doc documents by name elsewhere are Orbital Inferno, Savage Flame, Inferno Sphere and Salamander Mischief; all four were re-checked against maplestorywiki on 2026-09-12 and exist. Their relative order is the gap, not their identity.

priority.node: Common nodes: Erda Nova first, then Will of Erda / Blink / True Arachnid Reflection / Solar Crest, then Rope Lift
priority.why: Step 4 of the class doc's levelling order, given as a literal three-tier numbered list. Re-read verbatim on 2026-09-12 and it matches exactly: tier 1 Erda Nova, tier 2 Will of Erda + Blink + True Arachnid Reflection + Solar Crest, tier 3 Rope Lift. The doc's own reason for Erda Nova first is that it becomes the primary bind at Level 25, where its cooldown drops to 120 seconds, and that it is preferred over Cinder Maelstrom because the cast cannot whiff.

trios.why: mystyjl's cross-class node table gives Blaze Wizard this exact primary trio, verbatim: 'Orbital Flame, Blazing Extinction, Phoenix Drive'. Grandis independently puts Orbital Flame (Node 1) and Blazing Extinction (Node 2) alone in its Primary tier, on the stated grounds that those are the nodes that unlock 6th Job HEXA Mastery. CAVEAT, stated so the pairing is not read as unanimous: Grandis places Phoenix Drive in its SECONDARY tier (Node 3, with Orbital Explosion), not in Primary. The trio pairing of Phoenix Drive with the other two comes from mystyjl alone.
trios.consensusNote: Downgraded from strong on 2026-09-12. Two independent lineages agree that Orbital Flame and Blazing Extinction lead; the three-skill grouping itself has one. Nothing here reaches the 3-lineage bar for strong.

trios.why: mystyjl gives this exact second trio, verbatim: 'Towering Inferno, Cataclysm, Orbital Explosion'. Grandis's Secondary tier is Node 3 (Orbital Explosion, Phoenix Drive) and Node 4 (Towering Inferno, Cataclysm), which contains all three of these plus Phoenix Drive, and which Grandis describes as frequently used but not HEXA-unlocking.
trios.consensusNote: Downgraded from strong on 2026-09-12 under the 3-lineage rule.

trios.why: Grandis's lowest tier, re-read verbatim on 2026-09-12: 'Other nodes have lower priority - Node 5: Flame Tempest, Blazing Blitz, Cinder Maelstrom; Node 6: Flame Bite, Flame Vortex'. Grandis numbers exactly six boost-node groupings and these five skills occupy groups 5 and 6, which lines up with the class doc's 'Last two can be ignored, not part of any boost'. The doc does not name them, so that correspondence remains inference - well supported, but not asserted as sourced.

vMatrix.notes: GAP, flagged deliberately and re-confirmed on 2026-09-12 by reading the class doc's raw text export: the job-node ordering line renders the skill names as inline images, so the export returns the sentence with the names stripped ('Prioritize    followed by    and   , then   '). No job-node order is recorded here rather than guess at it. WARNING for anyone re-running this: an LLM summariser asked to read that line will confidently fill the blanks in with skill names taken from the table above it. That output is an extraction artifact, not the doc's answer. The real routes to the order are OCR of the Cookbook's images, or the Blaze Wizard Discord. Separately, the only boost-node opinion outside the class-doc lineage (mystyjl) self-reports 'Last Updated: November 21st, 2024', and Grandis's page carries a 'View Pre-V.269 Boost Nodes' toggle - direct evidence that groupings changed at v269 - so mystyjl's agreement with Grandis is reassuring but not proof of currency. Both facts re-verified on the live pages 2026-09-12.

order.step: Eternity (Origin) is the class's main burst payload
order.why: Class doc, verbatim: 'Big damage-over-time burst skill that lasts 30 seconds. MOST OF THE DAMAGE IS FRONTLOADED. Can bind twice; initial cast and when phoenix swoops down.' The doc does not state, in extractable text, where in the levelling order it sits.

order.step: Flame Concerto (Ascent) serves as supplementary finishing damage
order.why: Class doc, verbatim: '3x use per boss, unscaled damage, mostly useful for finishing boss phases without spending a burst. Does actually reduce the cooldown on Towering Inferno, which is assumed to be a bug.'

order.step: Sol Janus is left out of the bossing HEXA priority entirely; unlock it at level 1 early anyway
order.why: Class doc, verbatim, immediately under the heading 'HEXA Leveling Priority For Bossing.': 'Sol Janus is not included as it does not deal damage in bossing. Unlock Level 1 Janus as soon as possible. Leveling further entirely depends on your playstyle and choice of map in farming.' The doc separately describes it as having two modes, Dawn and Dusk, with different use cases, and as 'Disabled in most bossing content'.

order.step: Sol Hecate is the bossing-side common node, and its value arrives at named levels
order.why: Class doc, verbatim: 'A multipurpose skill that adds a variety of benefits to bossing.' Its three effects unlock at stated levels - Styx at Level 1 (a 4 second bind on a 1 minute cooldown that can extend bind timers and enable binding in the mini-burst), Charon at Level 20 (a door that activates on death granting a 10 second i-frame), Phlegethon at Level 30 (a larger burst of damage on a 2 minute cooldown). Those level gates are the only levelling-position information the doc gives for Sol Hecate in extractable text; it never states where the skill sits in the overall order.

heroicVsInteractive.claim: The class doc publishes two separate HEXA levelling charts under the headings 'Heroic Worlds (Fragment Gated)' and 'Interactive Worlds (Sol Erda Gated)'. Both are captioned 'START AT TOP LEFT. READ LEFT TO RIGHT.' The level numbers in the two grids differ, so the sequences are not the same.
heroicVsInteractive.why: Heroic and Interactive bottleneck on different currencies, so the efficient order is not the same. For a Heroic (Reboot) planner the fragment-gated chart is the relevant one. Both headings and both grids were read directly in the doc's text export on 2026-09-12; the numbers survive the export, the skill icons do not.

hexaStat.claim: The first three HEXA Stat cores should carry Magic ATT, INT and Critical Damage, in any order between them. Beyond that the doc sends the reader to an external optimiser because the answer is character-specific.
hexaStat.why: Class doc, verbatim, under the heading HEXA STAT: 'HEXA Stat's stat priority is character dependent. Ideally you use something like MapleScouter or MapleStory HEXA Stat Calculator in order to calculate your ideal HEXA Stat configuration. For picking the specific stats when unlocking, your first three cores (currently unlocked) should have Magic Attack, Int, and Critical Damage in any order.'
hexaStat.orderedNote: The three stats are an UNORDERED set. The doc says 'in any order' in as many words. Do not let array position be read as priority.

hexa.notes: MAJOR GAP, re-confirmed 2026-09-12 against the doc's raw text export rather than a summariser. The Arsonist's Cookbook does carry full HEXA levelling orders - one grid for Heroic, one for Interactive - but they are image grids in which only the target level numbers survive extraction (the export returns bare runs like '1 / (1) 20 / 4 / 6 / 1-3 / ... / 30'). The skill each number belongs to is an icon. So no step-by-step order is recorded here. The doc also links a 'BW Hexa Tracker v.271' and mentions alternative, more 'symmetric' orders below the images; neither is extractable either. Do NOT fill this in from an aggregator, and do not infer the order from the Sixth Job description table's row order - that table is captioned as being 'for easier viewing' and is not stated to be the priority list. The routes to the real order are OCR of the Cookbook's HEXA infographics, the linked HEXA tracker, or the Blaze Wizard Discord. Note also that this class doc is the only source found with any Blaze Wizard HEXA judgement: Grandis Library's Blaze Wizard page has a 6th job skill preview but publishes no HEXA levelling or priority recommendation, re-checked 2026-09-12.

hyperStats.notes: Recorded as an explicit non-answer, not as missing data. The class doc's entire content under the heading 'Hyper Skill/Stat Allocation' on the stat side is one line, verbatim: 'Hyper Stat calculator because Hyper stats are individual and based on player progression.' It publishes no allocation and no ranking. This matches the wider community position that hyper stats are a per-character computation rather than a list; the operative tool is MathBro's Hyper Stat Optimizer. Any fixed Blaze Wizard hyper stat order presented elsewhere should be treated as a simplification, not as sourced class judgement. Downstream code must not synthesise an order here - priority is null on purpose and ordered is false.

passives.orderedNote: An unordered set of five. Neither source ranks them against each other; all five are taken. Array position carries no meaning.
passives.why: Class doc, verbatim: 'You want all three Orbital Flame passives, Blazing Extinction - Add Attack, and Blazing Extinction - Reinforce.' Grandis states the same build: 'Orbital Flame - Range, Guard Break and Split Attack' and 'Blazing Extinction - Reinforce and Add Attack'. Effects, per the wiki, re-checked 2026-09-12: Range increases Orbital Flame's travel distance by 100 while toggled, Guardbreak gives Ignore Defense +20%, Split Attack is Damage -90%p / Number of Attacks +1, Reinforce adds damage, Add Attack adds an attack line. All five names appear on the wiki exactly as written here.
passives.consensusNote: Downgraded from moderate on 2026-09-12. The two pages stating this build are one lineage - Grandis credits 'Class Doc' under the heading that covers its Hyper Passive Build. The wiki independently confirms all five skills exist with these exact names and effects, but it carries no recommendation, so it does not raise the count. One lineage, therefore weak, therefore label it weak: the recommendation is probably right and is certainly not corroborated.

skip.why: These are the remaining four hyper passives on the class - the wiki's skill table lists exactly nine, and the five above plus these four account for all of them (re-enumerated from the wiki page on 2026-09-12). Neither source that publishes a build includes any of these four. Recorded as not-taken rather than as a judgement against them; no source argues against them explicitly.

actives.name: Phoenix Drive
actives.what: 20 second area attack around the character, 120 second cooldown. The class doc notes its duration can be stretched by server lag, and treats that interaction as the reason to target specific buff duration values.

actives.name: Cataclysm
actives.what: Large hit that leaves the character invincible and rooted through a roughly 5 second cast, 100 second cooldown. Doubles as an i-frame; the class doc adds that you can flash jump out afterward and retain a small amount of invincibility due to server lag.

actives.name: Glory of the Guardians
actives.what: 60 second +10% damage party buff, 120 second cooldown, applying only to Cygnus Knights and Mihile in the party. The class doc's entry reads 'Burst buff. Also synergizes with other Cygnus Knights in the party.'

hyperSkills.activesNote: Not a choice. The wiki lists exactly these three hyper actives for Blaze Wizard and they unlock at separate levels (140 / 160 / 190) without competing for a budget, so all three are taken. No source presents a selection decision here; the app should not render one. Level requirements re-checked on the wiki 2026-09-12.
hyperSkills.notes: Relevant to a Lv 140 character specifically: of the five recommended passives, only Orbital Flame - Range and Blazing Extinction - Reinforce are available at 140. Guardbreak needs 150; Add Attack and Split Attack need 180. Phoenix Drive is the only hyper active available at 140. Derived directly from the level requirements on the wiki's skill table (Range 140, Guardbreak 150, Split Attack 180, Reinforce 140, Spread 165, Add Attack 180, Orbital Explosion - Critical Chance 150, Orbital Explosion - Guardbreak 165, Orbital Explosion - Reinforce 190).

innerAbility.rankBasis: The class doc prints the bossing and farming builds as a two-column table, three rows deep, one row per inner ability line. The rank numbers below are that printed row order, and they line up with what the inner ability system actually allows: Passive Skills +1 is a first-line-only roll, and Boss Damage 10% is a second/third-line value (the first-line value is 20%, recorded under alternatives). So rank here means line slot as the doc printed it, not a strength ranking the doc states in words.

bossing.why: Class doc, verbatim: 'Passive Skills +1 gives a few extra stats but the only really notable parts are +3% final damage and +1% mastery from Pure Magic and 1% damage from Burning Conduit.' Grandis lists the same line.
bossing.consensusNote: Downgraded from moderate on 2026-09-12. Grandis credits 'Class Doc' under the heading covering its Inner Ability build, so the two pages are one lineage.

bossing.why: Class doc bossing column row 2, verbatim 'Boss Damage 10%'. Grandis lists 'Boss Damage +10%'. The two agree exactly on this line.
Class doc bossing column row 3, verbatim 'Abnormal Status Damage 8%'. Grandis words it 'Damage to monsters inflicted with Abnormal Status +8%' - same value, same line.

farming.line: Meso Obtained or Item Drop Rate +20%
farming.why: Class doc farming column row 1, verbatim '20% Meso/Item Drop'. Grandis: 'Meso Obtained / Item Drop Rate +20%'. Agree.

farming.line: The other of Item Drop Rate / Meso Obtained, +15%
farming.why: Class doc farming column row 2, verbatim '15% Item/Meso Drop'. Grandis: 'Meso Obtained / Item Drop Rate +15%'. Agree.

farming.line: Damage to Normal Monsters - value disputed between sources: +10% (class doc, v2.31 / GMS v.271) or +8% (Grandis, GMS Ver. 269)
farming.why: The line itself is agreed; the number is not. Class doc farming column row 3 reads verbatim '10% Normal Monster Damage'. Grandis's training build reads 'Damage to Normal Monsters +8%'. Both re-read on the live pages 2026-09-12. The doc is the newer of the two (v.271 against Grandis's Ver. 269) and is the lineage Grandis credits, so 10% is the value to prefer, but the disagreement is recorded rather than smoothed over - it is also evidence that Grandis is not a purely verbatim restatement of the doc.

alternatives.why: Class doc, under 'Alternative Options', verbatim: 'Boss 20% - An alternative to Passive Skills +1, if you roll this first, you can start rolling for Passive Skills +1 on a different Inner Ability preset.' This is the first-line Boss Damage value, which is why it substitutes for Passive Skills +1 rather than for the rank 2 line.
Class doc, verbatim: 'Magic Attack +21 - Line that gives more damage. Worse than the alternatives.' Recorded with the doc's own deprioritisation attached so it is not presented as an equal option.

Class doc, verbatim: 'Buff Duration +38% - Increases the duration of Terms and Conditions, enabling it to boost more of the burst and to alleviate hitting the requirement of 100% Buff Duration. Mostly useful if you do not have the Legion level to support getting 100% Buff Duration.' Conditional, not general: it is the fallback for a character whose Legion cannot reach the buff duration target.

innerAbility.notes: CLASS-SPECIFIC POINT, and it is the one that differs from generic mage advice: Attack Speed +1 appears nowhere in the Blaze Wizard inner ability recommendation - not in the bossing column, not in the farming column, not in the alternatives. Re-verified against the doc's raw text 2026-09-12. The reason is in the doc's fifth job Decent Skills entry: 'Decent Speed Infusion is required to hit Attack Speed 10', i.e. the class reaches the attack speed cap from a node rather than from an inner ability line, which frees the top line for damage. The cross-class inner ability rule of taking attack speed when a class lacks a Hurricane-type skill therefore does not apply here. Consensus on the lines themselves is weak, not moderate: Grandis restates the class doc for inner ability by its own crediting, so all six lines rest on one opinion, and no genuinely independent second opinion on Blaze Wizard inner ability was reachable in either session.

gearingNotes: Four things change gear and stat targets for Blaze Wizard specifically: the class brings 40% critical rate from its own passives, so it needs less crit from gear than most; part of that crit is conditional on holding a Wand; buff duration has hard breakpoints driven by Phoenix Drive and Burning Conduit rather than being a generic nice-to-have; and the attack speed cap is reached without spending an inner ability line on it. Each claim is itemised with its own sources in gearingClaims. NOTE: this section is outside the endgame scope of the 2026-09-12 resolution pass and was NOT re-verified; two open defects against gearingClaims[1] remain in contest.defects.

gearingClaims.claim: Blaze Wizard starts from 40% critical rate out of its own passives, so the remaining 60% has to come from links, Legion, hyper stats and gear. The class doc names Legion Artifact (+20%) and the Focus Spirit link (+10%) among the sources used to close the gap.
gearingClaims.why: Counting the wiki's own numbers gives the same 40%: Burning Focus +30%, Word of Fire +5%, Natural Talent +5%. The doc's figure and the wiki's skill data agree without either citing the other.

gearingClaims.claim: 5% of that base critical rate is conditional on the weapon: Natural Talent grants Critical Rate +5% only while a Wand is equipped.
gearingClaims.why: Stated on the skill itself. It means a staff-holding Blaze Wizard sits 5% crit below the doc's baseline and has to source that elsewhere. Neither the class doc nor Grandis addresses wand-versus-staff choice, so no recommendation is made here - only the mechanical fact.
gearingClaims.disputeNote: Two open defects against this entry (contest.defects) - the 'neither source addresses wand vs staff' statement and the 5%-below-baseline inference. Out of scope for the 2026-09-12 endgame resolution pass; left untouched deliberately, not endorsed.

gearingClaims.claim: Attack speed reaches the cap (stage 10 / AS0) with Decent Speed Infusion, even though not every Blaze Wizard skill benefits, because the rest of the kit gains from shorter cast times.
gearingClaims.why: This is why the bossing inner ability build spends its top line on Passive Skills +1 instead of Attack Speed +1. The wiki independently shows the class carries +2 attack speed on Word of Fire, +1 on Spell Control and +1 from Burning Conduit, which is consistent with reaching the cap cheaply.

gearingClaims.claim: Buff duration has named breakpoints rather than a smooth curve. The class doc gives 50% as the floor needed to hold Burning Conduit up, 95% as the value that best exploits Phoenix Drive's lag extension, 100% as nominally stronger but less consistent, and 101% or more as introducing an extra forced Phoenix Drive extension endpoint.
gearingClaims.why: The 50% floor checks out arithmetically against the wiki's numbers: Burning Conduit runs 40 seconds on a 60 second cooldown, so +50% duration takes it to 60 seconds and closes the gap. That is independent corroboration of the class doc's breakpoint from a source with no judgement content of its own.

gearingClaims.claim: IED targets given as visual (in-window) values, excluding passive sources: 92% for bosses with 300% PDR, 97% for bosses with 380% PDR.
gearingClaims.why: The exclusion matters because Fires of Creation contributes up to 30% ignore defense while a fire essence is summoned and the Orbital Flame - Guardbreak hyper adds 20%, so the number shown on gear is not the number that lands.

commonMistakes.mistake: Assuming Flashfire's return teleport always fires
commonMistakes.detail: The class doc warns that poor latency can cause the teleport back to the fire trail not to happen.
commonMistakes.disputeNote: Open defect (contest.defects): the underlying ping warning is real but the 'return teleport' and 'fire trail' framing is not in any source. Out of scope for the 2026-09-12 endgame pass; left untouched deliberately, not endorsed. Do not surface this entry to players until it is rewritten.

commonMistakes.mistake: Believing flash jumping grants Dark Sight
commonMistakes.detail: The class doc states plainly that the in-game skill description is wrong on this point and that no Dark Sight is granted.

commonMistakes.mistake: Not knowing when Phoenix Run triggers
commonMistakes.detail: The class doc's point is that a player who does not track the revive's activation window tends to waste the life it just gave back. Per the wiki the skill teleports backward on a fatal hit, restores up to 50% HP, grants 3 seconds of damage immunity, sits on a 1800 second cooldown and is not affected by cooldown reset.

commonMistakes.mistake: Treating Flashfire like an ordinary flash jump
commonMistakes.detail: The class doc flags its movement as floatier than most classes' flash jumps and says that difference kills players who are used to other classes.
commonMistakes.disputeNote: Open defect (contest.defects): the doc attributes the floatier movement to Firewalk, a different skill, not to Flashfire. Out of scope for the 2026-09-12 endgame pass; left untouched deliberately, not endorsed. Do not surface this entry to players until the skill name is corrected.

commonMistakes.mistake: Filling the HEXA order in from a generic aggregator
commonMistakes.detail: A research mistake rather than a gameplay one, recorded because it is the likely failure mode for this class. The pages that rank for Blaze Wizard HEXA queries are undated content-farm material recycling one cross-class ordering. The real Blaze Wizard order exists only as infographics inside the class doc and the class Discord. Re-confirmed 2026-09-12: an LLM summariser pointed at the class doc's HEXA section will also invent an order from the surrounding description table, which is the same failure in a different costume.

sources.what: Arsonist's Cookbook: A Comprehensive Guide to Blaze Wizard - the Blaze Wizard Discord's maintained class doc. Written (mostly) by Reeche (discord: reecheing, NA Kronos - Alpenrose). The only source carrying Blaze Wizard HEXA, node levelling, buff duration, crit and IED judgement. Fetch it as /export?format=txt and follow the single-use redirect immediately, OR curl it with -L, which follows the redirect and returns the raw text (the reliable route - use this rather than an LLM summariser, which will hallucinate skill names into the image-stripped gaps).
sources.dated: Version 2.31 (9/10/2026) - GMS v.271 (Frieren Collab), read from the doc's own header line on 2026-09-12

sources.what: Grandis Library Blaze Wizard page. Boost node tiering (Primary Node 1-2 / Secondary Node 3-4 / Other Node 5-6), hyper skill passive build, recommended inner ability split for bossing and training, link skill, base stats from skills. Has a 6th job skill preview but NO HEXA levelling or priority recommendation.
sources.dated: GMS Ver. 269 [Ride the Lightning Update] - two patches behind the v.271 target. Re-read on the live page 2026-09-12.
sources.independenceNote: Re-verified 2026-09-12 on the page itself: Grandis credits 'Class Doc' under the heading 'Inner Ability + Hyper Passive Build + Boost Nodes Build'. For Blaze Wizard that doc is the Arsonist's Cookbook, so Grandis agreeing with the Cookbook on those three fields is one source agreeing with itself. Counted as a restatement, not a vote. It is not a verbatim restatement, though - its training build says Damage to Normal Monsters +8% where the doc says 10%.

sources.what: mastermysty's cross-class boost node trio reference. Gives Blaze Wizard a primary trio of Orbital Flame / Blazing Extinction / Phoenix Drive and a secondary of Towering Inferno / Cataclysm / Orbital Explosion, with no bossing-versus-mobbing split for this class. Re-read 2026-09-12, both trios confirmed verbatim. The only boost-node opinion found that is genuinely outside the class-doc lineage.
sources.caveat: Predates the v269 boost-node regrouping. Treated as corroboration of the grouping, never as the sole source.

sources.what: Name and number validation table. Used to confirm every skill, node and hyper passive name written into this file, their level requirements, and the numeric values behind the crit rate, attack speed and buff duration claims. Carries zero judgement, so it never raises a recommendation's sourceCount. Returns 403 to WebFetch; curl with a normal browser User-Agent returns 200.
sources.dated: living wiki; revision date not verifiable (page history was not reachable)

sources.what: Cross-class inner ability framework. Used only to note which of its class-shape rules does not apply to Blaze Wizard.

Blaze Wizard class Discord - origin of the Arsonist's Cookbook and the place the HEXA infographics live. Not readable by this agent. This is where the missing HEXA order and job-node order have to come from.

TajMaJon's Blaze Wizard video guide, linked from Grandis Library. NOT USED as a source in this file: TajMaJon is credited on the Arsonist's Cookbook, so it is the same lineage restated. Listed so it is not mistaken for a fourth opinion later.
MathBro's Hyper Stat Optimizer. Cited only to support the recorded position that Blaze Wizard hyper stats are computed per character rather than ranked in a fixed list.
sources.dated: actively maintained; exact last update not confirmed

consensusLevelNote: Lowered from moderate on 2026-09-12. Under the independence model recorded above, every endgame recommendation for this class rests on one lineage except the boost node trios, which rest on two. Nothing reaches three.

positions: Counting pages, Blaze Wizard looks well covered: a current class doc, a Grandis page, a cross-class node table and a wiki.

Counting lineages, it is thinner. Grandis credits the class doc in as many words for inner ability, hyper passives and boost nodes, so those three fields rest on ONE opinion. Only the boost-node grouping has a second, independent vote (mystyjl), and that source is from 2024.
conflicts.resolution: Not resolved, and now reflected in the labels rather than only in prose: every affected claim carries sourceCount 1 and consensus weak as of 2026-09-12.

positions: mystyjl's trio table (last updated November 21st, 2024) and Grandis (GMS Ver. 269) describe the same grouping, which suggests it is stable.

Grandis exposes a 'View Pre-V.269 Boost Nodes' toggle, which is direct evidence that boost-node groupings changed at v269. A 2024 table agreeing with a v269 page is therefore either genuine stability or a coincidence nobody has re-checked.
conflicts.resolution: Not resolved. Flagged rather than picked. Both the mystyjl date and the Grandis toggle were re-verified on the live pages 2026-09-12.

positions: Class doc (v2.31, GMS v.271): '10% Normal Monster Damage'.
Grandis Library (GMS Ver. 269): 'Damage to Normal Monsters +8%'.
conflicts.resolution: Prefer 10%: the class doc is the newer document and is the lineage Grandis credits. Recorded rather than smoothed over, and noted as evidence that Grandis is not a purely verbatim restatement. Found by the contest pass and confirmed against both live pages 2026-09-12.

positions: 95% is the value the class doc recommends, because it most reliably exploits Phoenix Drive's lag extension.
100% is, in the same doc's framing, nominally the stronger number, but it is described as less consistent in practice.
conflicts.resolution: This is a tension the source itself records, not a disagreement between sources. Both values are carried.

gaps: HEXA levelling order, both the Heroic fragment-gated and Interactive Sol Erda-gated charts - present in the class doc only as numbered image grids. Confirmed again 2026-09-12 by reading the raw text export: only the target level numbers survive, the skill each belongs to is an icon. Needs OCR, the doc's linked BW Hexa Tracker v.271, or a Discord pull.

Job-node levelling order within the V matrix - same problem. The four class skill nodes are known and verified (Orbital Inferno, Savage Flame, Inferno Sphere, Salamander Mischief); only their order is missing.
Hyper stat allocation - deliberately not published by the source; treat as a calculator problem, not a missing list.
Legion effect for Blaze Wizard - not sourced in any session so far.
Secondary weapon type - not sourced in any session so far.

No independent second opinion on inner ability, hyper passives or HEXA. Grandis is the same lineage as the class doc by its own crediting, so those fields have exactly one opinion behind them. r/Maplestory remains unchecked for this class.

contest.method: An independent agent re-searched every claim in this file without seeing the researcher's reasoning, and was instructed to refute rather than confirm.

resolutionPass.scope: Endgame only, per product owner narrowing: vMatrix, hexa, hyperSkills, hyperStats, innerAbility. Defects concerning jobs 1-4 skills, gearing, coefficients or rotations were classified out of scope and their content left untouched.
resolutionPass.method: Every cited page was re-opened. The class doc was pulled as raw text with curl -L rather than through a summarising fetch, after a summarising fetch was caught inventing job-node names ('Orbital Inferno, Savage Flame, and Inferno Sphere first') to fill the doc's image-stripped ordering line. Grandis, mystyjl and maplestorywiki were re-read directly. Every endgame claim was then relabelled under an explicit independence model recorded at independenceModel.
resolutionPass.outcome: 1 in-scope defect resolved. 4 defects classified out of scope and left open. 0 endgame claims deleted - every endgame claim in the file turned out to be supported by the source it cited. 13 endgame claims were relabelled DOWNWARD because their consensus labels overstated the independence of the evidence: two 'strong' trio labels became 'moderate', and every doc-plus-Grandis claim became 'weak' with sourceCount 1.

resolved.defect: UNRECORDED SOURCE CONFLICT - innerAbility.farming rank 3 is given as 'Damage to Normal Monsters +10%' from the class doc (doc text: '10% Normal Monster Damage'). Grandis's training build says '+8%'. The file records no conflict.
resolved.action: Re-read both live pages 2026-09-12. The class doc's farming column row 3 does read '10% Normal Monster Damage'; Grandis's training build does read 'Damage to Normal Monsters +8%'. The claim now states both values and which to prefer (10%, the newer document and the lineage Grandis credits), and a new entry was added to conflicts. The critic's secondary observation - that this proves Grandis is not a verbatim restatement - was folded into the Grandis source note in both directions: it is still the same lineage for crediting purposes, but it is not a copy.

resolved.action: Every endgame claim was checked against the page it cites and all of them are supported. The one place worth naming: vMatrix.trios primary lists Phoenix Drive alongside Orbital Flame and Blazing Extinction and cites Grandis, but Grandis puts Phoenix Drive in its SECONDARY tier. The old 'why' text was technically careful about this; it is now stated outright so the citation cannot be read as Grandis endorsing the trio. Likewise vMatrix.trios other now says in plain terms that the link between Grandis's node groups 5-6 and the class doc's 'last two can be ignored' is inference, not a sourced statement.

defects: OUT OF SCOPE (commonMistakes, not an endgame section) - FABRICATED MECHANIC - commonMistakes[0] "Assuming Flashfire's return teleport always fires ... the teleport back to the fire trail". No source says this. The Cookbook describes Flashfire as an installed teleport, repositionable by downcasting, usable in air, no range limit, lasting 100 seconds, and says only that on bad ping it "will occasionally fail to teleport you". There is no return teleport and no fire trail in the mechanic; the trail belongs to Blazing Blitz per the wiki. The underlying ping warning is real; the mechanical description around it is invented. STATUS: left untouched per the endgame-only scope, but flagged inline with disputed:true so it cannot be surfaced as verified.

OUT OF SCOPE (commonMistakes, not an endgame section) - MISATTRIBUTED SKILL - commonMistakes[3] "Treating Flashfire like an ordinary flash jump ... floatier than most classes' flash jumps". The Cookbook attributes that to Firewalk, a different skill: "Blaze Wizard's version of the Cygnus flash jump. Floatier (goes further but slower velocity)", which also passively caps Speed/Jump. Firewalk is confirmed as its own skill on the wiki (Active, Master Level 5). The file never mentions Firewalk and pins its behaviour on Flashfire. STATUS: left untouched per the endgame-only scope, but flagged inline with disputed:true.

OUT OF SCOPE (gearingClaims, not an endgame section) - FALSE STATEMENT ABOUT A SOURCE - gearingClaims[1] says "Neither the class doc nor Grandis addresses wand-versus-staff choice, so no recommendation is made here". The Cookbook's Equip Window section addresses it directly and recommends a staff for the higher Magic ATT, saying that with newer crit sources such as Legion Artifact the wand's small crit niche is largely unnecessary. A real, sourceable class judgement was recorded as absent. STATUS: left untouched per the endgame-only scope, but flagged inline with disputed:true.

OUT OF SCOPE (gearingClaims, not an endgame section) - WRONG DERIVED INFERENCE - gearingClaims[1] concludes "a staff-holding Blaze Wizard sits 5% crit below the doc's baseline and has to source that elsewhere". Backwards. The doc's 40% baseline is built without the wand (Base 5% + Word of Fire 5% + Burning Focus 30%) and lists Wand +5% as an additional optional source. A staff user sits AT the baseline; a wand user sits 5% above it. The wand-conditional +5% on Natural Talent itself is real and correctly quoted from the wiki - only the inference drawn from it is wrong, and it is the kind of error that would make a planner tell staff users to buy crit they do not need. STATUS: left untouched per the endgame-only scope, but flagged inline with disputed:true. Worth fixing in a gearing pass - it is the most player-damaging of the four.
